main_text.l: CHARACTE-
RUM IESUITI-
CORUM CENTURIA
QUARTA, ex D. Augustini scriptis Polemicis collecta,
I.
Si quid tēporalis molestiæ passi fuerint
[ut de persecutione Anglicana tragicis & famosis
libellis passim hodie conqueruntur Iesuitæ]
per certissimum atq; rectissimum ordinem pote-
statum, cùm ipsis priuatis furiosorum agmini-
bus multa grauiora passim atq; quotidie, nulla
regia, nulla Ecclesiastica lege committant:
nos corporum persecutores vocant, sc anima-
rum interfectores non vocant, cùm priuata li-
centia corporibus parcant. Sed quia semper
per mansuetudinem Christianam multò seue-
rius oculus iudicatur cuiusus[?] in lite, quàm ani-
mus excæcatus in schismate, & aduersum nos
loquuntur, & nobiscum loquuntur: & cùm
eos obmutescere compellat veritas, silere non
permittit iniquitas. lib. 1. contra Epistolam Par-
II.
Tanto isti amore hominum cæci sunt, &
corde

page.notes: Two small "(" marks stand in the left margin beside the first paragraph; they are printer's marks or stray marks, not text, and were not transcribed. The word "cuiusus" (line 9 of paragraph I) is doubtful; it may be "cuiusuis" with a worn letter. The abbreviation over "temporalis" is read as a macron and may be a tilde. The page ends mid-sentence ("& corde"), and the sentence continues on the next page. No catchword is visible.
